analysis.architecture_style: 3-tier Windows monolith (ASP.NET WebForms + stored-procedure business logic)
analysis.summary: A server-rendered WebForms application on two sticky-session IIS servers, backed by a SQL Server 2012 database that holds most business rules in ~400 stored procedures. Instrument results arrive as CSV files on an SMB share and are polled by a separate Windows Service. Every core platform layer is past end of support.

risks.title: Loss of validated state during migration
risks.description: Moving OS, database and hosting invalidates existing IQ evidence; without a risk-based re-validation plan the system cannot be used for batch release.
risks.mitigation: Risk-based CSA plan: re-execute IQ on new infrastructure, targeted OQ on changed functions, PQ via parallel run across two batch-release cycles, QA sign-off gate before cutover.

risks.title: Unpatched end-of-life platform
risks.description: Windows Server 2012 R2 and SQL Server 2012 receive no security updates and are already an audit finding.
risks.mitigation: Make platform exit the wave-1 driver; isolate the servers in a restricted network segment until cutover.

risks.title: Hidden business logic in stored procedures
risks.description: ~400 undocumented stored procedures hold validated calculations; refactoring could silently change results.
risks.mitigation: Replatform procedures unchanged to Azure SQL Managed Instance; add characterisation tests before any refactor.

risks.title: Key-person dependency
risks.description: Only two developers understand the stored procedures and the integration service.
risks.mitigation: Embed both in the migration team from week 1 and document critical procedures during assessment.

risks.title: Instrument file integrity gap
risks.description: CSV files on the SMB share can be altered or deleted before ingestion and are not checksummed - an ALCOA+ gap.
risks.mitigation: Event-driven ingestion that hashes files on arrival, stores originals in immutable storage and writes an audit-trail entry.

risks.title: Cutover collides with batch release
risks.description: Downtime during month-end batch release would delay product release.
risks.mitigation: Mid-month cutover window, online migration with log-backup replay, rehearsed rollback plan.

risks.title: Cloud supplier not yet qualified
risks.description: GxP requires assessing the cloud provider as a supplier with a defined shared-responsibility model.
risks.mitigation: Use the provider's GxP guidance and audit reports (SOC 2, ISO 27001), sign a quality agreement and map shared responsibility in the validation plan.

risks.title: EU data residency breach
risks.description: Ireland-site records must stay in the EU; a single global deployment could breach residency commitments.
risks.mitigation: Deploy to an EU region with an allowed-locations policy and document data flows in the validation plan.

opportunities.title: Retire tape backups
opportunities.benefit: Automated geo-redundant backups with point-in-time restore cut RPO from 24 hours to minutes.

opportunities.title: Elastic capacity for month-end
opportunities.benefit: Scale the web tier out during batch release, ending month-end slowdowns.

opportunities.title: Validation as code
opportunities.benefit: Automated regression tests and infrastructure-as-code turn ~300 manual OQ scripts into repeatable evidence, in line with FDA's Computer Software Assurance approach.

opportunities.title: Onboard new sites in weeks
opportunities.benefit: A templated landing zone shrinks new-site onboarding from 3 months to a few weeks.

opportunities.title: Near real-time instrument results
opportunities.benefit: Event-driven ingestion delivers results in seconds and closes the data integrity gap.

plan.headline: Replatform LabTrack onto Azure PaaS in about 30 weeks, then strangle instrument ingestion and reporting into cloud-native services - preserving validated state through a risk-based IQ/OQ/PQ plan.

patterns.name: Replatform to managed PaaS
patterns.why: Fastest exit from the end-of-life OS and database while keeping validated stored-procedure logic unchanged.

patterns.name: Strangler fig
patterns.why: Peel off instrument ingestion and CoA reporting after the platform move, re-validating only what changes.

patterns.name: Event-driven ingestion
patterns.why: Replaces SMB polling with blob events, adding hashing and immutable storage for ALCOA+.

patterns.name: Externalised session state
patterns.why: Moving session state to a managed cache removes sticky sessions and enables scale-out.

component_strategies.rationale: Retarget to .NET Framework 4.8 and run on App Service; minimal code change keeps OQ scope small.
Near-full SQL Server compatibility keeps all stored procedures unchanged, with built-in HA and point-in-time restore.
Replace the polling Windows Service with event-driven ingestion that checksums files and writes audit entries.
Keep validated CoA templates during waves 1-2 to avoid re-validating report output; modernise reporting in the final phase.
component_strategies.target_service: App Service, then Power BI paginated reports

component_strategies.rationale: Replaced by an immutable blob landing container with checksums.
Empower stays on-premises in the labs; an upload agent sends exports to Azure over private connectivity.
SAP is out of scope; replace the flat-file hand-off with a scheduled pipeline.
Hybrid identity keeps unique user IDs for Part 11 and adds MFA on e-signatures.
A managed email service replaces the on-premises relay.

plan.target_summary: Azure PaaS in an EU region inside a GxP landing zone: App Service web tier with Redis session state, Azure SQL Managed Instance, event-driven instrument ingestion through Functions and immutable Blob Storage, Entra ID for identity, and Azure Monitor / Log Analytics for audit-grade logging.
